clue.text: Scan some card involved in method of finding data

indicators.note: letters that are involved are tangled up together, so the words before it are jumbled

blocks.note: the twelve letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone scans a card as part of a way of looking up records.
explanation.definitionFit: Random access is a computing term for retrieving stored data directly from any location without reading through everything before it.

clue.text: Summary concerning surrender

blocks.note: re is a formal word meaning about or with regard to
capitulation is the act of giving in to an enemy

explanation.surface: A short report about an army laying down its arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A recapitulation is a brief restatement of the main points, a recap, which is exactly what a summary provides.

clue.text: City with character portrayed in Oliver Twist

blocks.note: first meaning: a city in north-eastern France, in Lorraine
second meaning: the young woman in Dickens's novel who is killed by Bill Sikes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a single description of a place in Dickens, but the French city and the Dickens character simply share a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy is the capital of historic Lorraine in France, and also Bill Sikes's tragic companion in the Dickens novel.

clue.text: Chooses to screen one film for hopeful people

indicators.note: to screen something is to shield it behind you, so the first word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: opts means picks or chooses
I is the Roman numeral for one
a film here is a thin haze or layer, as of mist on a window

explanation.surface: A cinema chooses to screen one film to please its optimistic audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' and 'film' both pull toward the cinema; here a film is a thin hazy layer, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimists are those who expect good outcomes, so they are naturally described as people full of hope.

clue.text: Break down in twisting lane, say

indicators.note: something twisting is bent out of its shape, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters of both words are used

explanation.surface: A car breaks down on a winding country road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break down' suggests a vehicle failure; here it means to examine by separating into parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to separate it into its component parts for study, which is the figurative sense of breaking it down.

clue.text: Hypocrisy at heart of grand choral composition

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: cant is insincere, pious talk
taken as written
the middle letter of this five-letter word

explanation.surface: Hypocrisy lies at the centre of some grandiose choral work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' seems to describe the composition but only supplies its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a medium-length vocal piece for soloists and choir, often with orchestral accompaniment, as in Bach's church works.

clue.text: Good to follow inclination, having no time for jargon

indicators.note: one piece following another means it is placed after it in the answer
having no of something means it is taken away from the word built so far

blocks.note: a slant is a tilt or leaning
T is the standard abbreviation for time
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Advice that following one's inclinations is good, if there is no time for technical jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: SLANT loses its T, then G is added after.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary of a particular group, close in meaning to jargon, the specialist talk of insiders.

clue.text: Larks in a changing nation

indicators.note: letters that are changing are moving into a new order

blocks.note: all eight letters of these words

explanation.surface: Songbirds are in a country undergoing change.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island country off the southern tip of India, formerly known as Ceylon.

clue.text: Understandable background for scientific study

blocks.note: natural in the sense of to be expected, easily understood
someone's history is their past or background

explanation.surface: A reasonable grounding needed before taking up science.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural history is the study of plants and animals in their environment, a long-established branch of science.

clue.text: Compel prisoners to join procession

indicators.note: one group joining another means the two are put side by side

blocks.note: cons is slang for convicts
a train is a long line of people or vehicles moving along

explanation.surface: Inmates are forced to fall in with a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrain someone is to force or oblige them, so the verb matches compelling them to act.

clue.text: Main artery, part of great road to the west

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, a run of consecutive letters
in an across clue going west means running right to left, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A main highway is described as part of a great westbound road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main artery' looks like a highway, matching 'great road', but it is the body's largest blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the largest blood vessel, carrying blood from the heart's left ventricle to the rest of the body.

clue.text: Secretary with variable income

blocks.note: PA is short for personal assistant
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A secretary whose earnings fluctuate.
explanation.definitionFit: Pay is the wages or salary someone earns, the money coming in from work.

clue.text: A eulogy a man arranged for poet

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all eleven letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone organises a eulogy for a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Maya Angelou was an American poet and memoirist, author of I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings.

clue.text: Mediterranean port tests limits of trade

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters

blocks.note: tries means tests or tries out
the outside letters of this word

explanation.surface: A seaport puts the boundaries of commerce to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is an Italian port city at the head of the Adriatic, an arm of the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Year's aid distributed, presumably

indicators.note: something distributed is spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: all eight letters, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A year's worth of aid has probably been handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a conversational way of conceding something is likely, just as presumably signals a reasonable assumption.

clue.text: Before noon I moan, ordered to get cleaning fluid

indicators.note: ordered means put into a sequence, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, before midday
the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A cleaner grumbles each morning when told to go and fetch the cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia dissolved in water is a common household cleaner, used especially on glass and hard surfaces.

clue.text: Chap raised alarm over minute quirk

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word means reading it upwards, from bottom to top
in a down clue over means placed above, so the following piece comes beneath

blocks.note: a man, a fellow
a siren is a warning device
M is the abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A man sounds the alarm about some tiny eccentricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like the adjective tiny, but it is the unit of time abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannerism is a habitual gesture or way of speaking peculiar to someone, an idiosyncrasy or quirk.

clue.text: Worked together in trouble, back with struggling side

indicators.note: going back means the word before is read from its end
something struggling is thrashing about, so its letters are disordered

blocks.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
the letters of this word

explanation.surface: Teammates cooperated when in difficulty, backing up a side that was struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' and 'side' sound like football; 'in' is just the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and keep in contact with others, so the past tense matches having worked together.

clue.text: Old-fashioned hugs about to be given

indicators.note: to hug something is to wrap arms round it, so the first word encloses the next

blocks.note: dated means out of fashion
on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned embraces are about to be handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something donated has been given as a gift, typically to a charity or good cause.

clue.text: Under half of energy used to fill tub

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word means just its first three letters are taken
filling a vessel means putting something inside it

blocks.note: a bath is a tub for washing
the first half of this word

explanation.surface: Below the waterline, half one's energy goes on filling the bathtub.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath is a preposition meaning lower than or underneath, a direct synonym of under.

clue.text: Little left, nothing new, in ancient place

blocks.note: baby as an adjective means very small
L is the abbreviation for left
O looks like zero
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Little remains, and nothing new, of an ancient site.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon was a great city of ancient Mesopotamia on the Euphrates, famous for its hanging gardens.

clue.text: Subversive motive in chart

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another means it goes inside that other word

blocks.note: a table is a chart of figures
a reason is a motive for doing something

explanation.surface: A seditious motive is hidden in a diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something treasonable betrays one's country or aims to overthrow the state, which is what subversive activity does.

clue.text: County fielder endlessly on move

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut off
in a down clue on means placed on top of the next piece

blocks.note: slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper
a go is a turn or move in a game

explanation.surface: A county cricketer keeps moving about the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county on the north-west coast of the Republic of Ireland, named after its main town.

clue.text: Used to be necessary to know a subject

blocks.note: first meaning: the past tense of the verb to be
second meaning, cryptic: this verb form cannot stand alone, so a speaker must name who or what it refers to

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a grammar joke: 'was' only makes sense with a subject such as I, he or it in front of it, so a subject must be known.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past form of being for I, he, she or it, so it describes what once existed or used to be.

clue.text: Vehicle secured with load of silver

indicators.note: carrying a load means holding cargo inside, so the first word holds the next

blocks.note: to have won something is to have secured it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A truck carrying silver bullion is locked up safely.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a wheeled cart for carrying goods, typically horse-drawn, and so a vehicle.

clue.text: Fine area, quiet one for ruminant

blocks.note: OK means fine, all right
A is the abbreviation for area
p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A pleasant, quiet patch of ground suits a grazing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a cud-chewing African mammal related to the giraffe, and cud-chewers are classed as ruminants.

clue.text: Lecture from ruler occupying total broadcast

indicators.note: to occupy a place is to sit inside it, so the first word goes within the rearranged one
broadcast means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of this word, shuffled
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch gives a speech while taking over a whole radio network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' fits the lecture picture but signals that TOTAL is jumbled around KING.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a reprimand or scolding, which is the sense of lecture as a telling-off.

clue.text: Failing doctor with desire reflected in notes

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a business that is folding is failing and closing down
MO is medical officer
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A struggling doctor's wishes are recorded in written notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests a doctor's notes but means banknotes; yen also tempts as currency, yet it is the desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding money is paper currency, as opposed to coins, so it matches notes in the sense of banknotes.
